title: Two Ways to Pack Atoms
question: How can atoms be locked in place and still make such different solids?
hook: Diamond and glass are both rigid, yet their atoms are arranged in opposite ways.
idea: Solids hold their atoms tightly in place, either in a regular lattice or in an irregular arrangement.

beats.prompt: A hiker steps from solid rock onto loose lunar dust, and it gives way. Why?

choices.label: Each grain is a softer material than rock
choices.feedback: Tempting, but changes in individual particles are still greatly hindered.

choices.label: The grains slip past one another easily
The dust is really a liquid in disguise
choices.feedback: Tempting, but the grains are solid particles that merely slide past one another.

beats.explain: In a solid aggregate such as sand or dust, the particles slip past one another, which gives a perceived softness and ease of compression.

beats.prompt: Put the steps of water bursting a steel container in order
items: Water in a rigid container gradually freezes
The ice takes up more volume than the water did
With no room to expand, the ice presses hard on the container's interior
The container explodes with great force
beats.explain: Ice is less dense than water, so it needs more room. In a rigid container it has nowhere to go, so it pushes outward until the container gives way.

beats.prompt: Match each material to how its atoms are arranged
beats.explain: Some solids keep a regular order across a whole piece, many are made of many small crystals, and others have no long-range order at all.

beats.prompt: Sort each solid by how its atoms are arranged
beats.explain: Crystalline solids have regular geometric lattices, while amorphous solids have irregular arrangements.
